questions.prompt: Does preparing an introduction make it inauthentic?
questions.answer: No; preparation can support honest communication.

questions.prompt: Is authenticity identical to complete disclosure?
questions.answer: No; privacy and role boundaries are compatible with honesty.
No; factual accuracy and accountability still matter.

questions.prompt: How should a commitment be evaluated?
questions.answer: By feasibility, honesty and observable follow-through.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Communicates truthful capabilities and values with contextual adaptation, privacy and realistic commitments.
scoring.transfer: Complete the introduction and feedback capstone: demonstrate accurate attention, context-appropriate humour or plain speech, an engaging factual story and a truthful introduction. Include recipient choice, a correction after feedback and one privacy boundary.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
